verdicts.title: DPTrainer documents per-group clipping_norm keys as regex when they are plain substrings, and offers no allow_unused_patterns escape hatch
verdicts.reasoning: Every link verified in the current tree. docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md:92-93 still says clipping_norm accepts 'a dict keyed by regex on parameter names with a "fallback" entry'; grep shows 'regex' appears nowhere else in the huggingface docs or clipping.md. packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:1531-1546 pops 'fallback' and forwards the remaining keys verbatim as per_group_clipper(trainable_params, fallback=fb, **patterns) with no re.compile and no allow_unused_patterns. packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_per_group.py:141-142 matches with 'matches = [pat for pat in all_patterns if pat in display]' -- plain substring containment. Ran it: per_group({...}, fallback=1.0, **{'model\\.layers\\.\\d+\\.self_attn': 0.1}) raises ConfigurationError('Patterns did not match any parameter: ...'), and per_group over layers.0/1/2/10/11 with pattern 'layers.1' assigns layers.1, layers.10 AND layers.11 to the 'layers.1' group while layers.0/layers.2 fall through to fallback -- i.e. the substring rule silently widens a doc-following user's intent. grep confirms allow_unused_patterns exists only in opaque-engine source/tests and docs/user-guide/clipping.md:373; nothing in opaque-transformers plumbs it, so the 'one config across architectures' case is unreachable from TrainingArguments. docs/user-guide/clipping.md:365-373 describes the substring rule correctly, so the two user-facing pages contradict each other. Two corrections to the finding's framing: (a) the failure is raised at train() time, not at trainer construction -- the clipping block lives in _setup_training (def at :1397), called from train() at :1188, so a DPTrainer(...) call succeeds and only trainer.train() raises; (b) severity stays low because the outcome today is fail-closed (ConfigurationError), not silent mis-grouping -- the residual harm is a doc that contradicts the code plus a missing escape hatch. Not present in milestones-open.tsv or other-open-issues.tsv.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user follows docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md:92-93 and passes clipping_norm={'model\\.layers\\.\\d+\\.self_attn': 0.1, 'fallback': 1.0}. Construction succeeds; trainer.train() raises ConfigurationError('Patterns did not match any parameter: [...]. Use allow_unused_patterns=True ...') from _per_group.py:170-177, because matching is substring containment ('pat in display'), not regex. Fail-closed, so no silent privacy loss -- the harm is that the error contradicts the documentation the user followed, that DPTrainer exposes no way to pass allow_unused_patterns for a deliberately-partial pattern set, and that the substring rule quietly widens intent for keys that do match: verified that pattern 'layers.1' with a fallback puts layers.1, layers.10 and layers.11 into one group while layers.0/layers.2 go to fallback, which changes PerGroup.effective = sqrt(sum v^2) and therefore the sensitivity the accountant is calibrated with.

verdicts.title: DDP resume collapses every rank's Poisson sampler stream to rank 0's, so co-indexed records across shards are perfectly co-included while the accountant still prices independent Poisson
verdicts.reasoning: Every link of the chain verified independently in the current tree, and the two quantitative claims reproduced exactly. (1) Fresh-run independence: _dp_trainer.py:3946-3950 does 'if self._ddp.world_size > 1: sampler_key = fold_in(sampler_key, self._ddp.rank)' inside the 'if ctx.current_sampler is None' branch. (2) Snapshot is written by one rank only: _save_dp_runtime (:5273-5310, which serialises ctx.current_sampler into the single DP_STATE_NAME file) is called at :5197 inside 'if _distributed.should_save(a, self._ddp)'; should_save (_distributed.py:211-222) is world-rank-0 by default. (3) The snapshot is read and applied by EVERY rank: the resume load at :1175-1178 is not rank-gated, and :1861-1877 runs 'ctx.current_sampler = from_state_dict(ctx.current_sampler, saved_sampler_state)' on every rank, overwriting the rank-folded template. (4) from_state_dict takes the stream key straight from the snapshot: _poisson.py:255-260 builds RngKey(seed=int(sd['key_seed']), impl=str(sd['key_impl'])) and uses the template only for data_source/n_steps; the same pattern exists in _k_out_of_t.py, dpftrl/_poisson.py, _b_min_sep.py, _balls_in_bins.py. (5) Ran the sampler-level repro myself: PoissonSampler(ds16, q=0.25) under fold_in(key(42),0) emits [[4,5,8],[1,5,9,14,15],[4,12,13]] and under fold_in(key(42),1) emits [[3,5,7,13,15],[0,6],[6,7,9,13]]; after both are rebuilt through from_state_dict with rank 0's snapshot they both emit [[4,5,8],[1,5,9,14,15],[4,12,13]] -- byte-identical, matching the finding's numbers. (6) Re-derived the magnitude myself by numerical hockey-stick integration at sigma=1, q=0.01, delta=1e-5: independent Poisson eps=0.19945, the W=2 correlated-group pair ((1-q)N(0)+qN(1) vs (1-q)N(0)+qN(2)) eps=2.39891, W=4 eps=3.13866 -- exactly the finding's 0.1995 / 2.3989 / 3.1387. (7) The accountant side is unchanged: :1489-1494 'The accountant uses regular acc.poisson over the global rate.' (8) No user-facing signal: docs/user-guide/distributed-trainer.md has no resume section, and no runtime warning is emitted; only an in-source comment at :3879-3885 acknowledges it ('resuming a DDP run currently restores rank 0's per-rank key on every rank ... tracked for the multi-GPU work'). That in-code acknowledgement does not correspond to any issue in milestones-open.tsv or other-open-issues.tsv (the only distributed entries there are FSDP2 #55-58, a different subsystem), so already_tracked=0. I did not re-run the full 2-rank gloo trainer resume the finder reports; the code chain plus the sampler-level repro settle it. The adjacent comment at :3871-3873 ('the per-record marginal stays Bernoulli(q) either way, so the privacy accounting is unaffected') is wrong as a justification -- subsampling amplification needs independence across records, not just the marginal. Severity high: silent, epsilon-affecting, on a supported default path (world_size>1 + resume_from_checkpoint after preemption), understating a realisable worst case by ~12x at W=2 in the configuration measured.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Multi-rank DDP (torchrun --nproc-per-node>=2) with checkpointing on, job preempted, restarted with resume_from_checkpoint. Each rank owns a disjoint local_shard (_dp_trainer.py:3909-3913) and on a fresh run draws an independent Bernoulli(q) mask because the rank is folded into the sampler key (:3949). The sampler snapshot, however, is written only by the saving rank (_save_dp_runtime under should_save, :5197) and restored unconditionally by every rank (:1875-1877), and every sampler family rebuilds its stream key verbatim from the snapshot (_poisson.py:259). Verified directly at the sampler level: two PoissonSamplers seeded with fold_in(key(42),0) / fold_in(key(42),1) emit different index lists, and after both are passed through from_state_dict with rank 0's snapshot they emit identical lists. After the resume point every rank therefore selects the same LOCAL offsets in its own shard, so the records sharing a local index across the W shards are included or excluded together with probability 1, while the accountant keeps pricing independent Poisson (acc.poisson at the global rate, :1494). Magnitude, re-derived here by numerical hockey-stick integration at sigma=1, q=0.01, delta=1e-5 for a single step: the intended independent Poisson mechanism gives eps=0.199; the neighbouring pair actually realisable with W=2 correlated records gives eps=2.399 (W=4: 3.139). No warning is emitted, distributed-trainer.md has no resume section, and only an in-source comment (:3879-3885) records the caveat.

verdicts.title: The distributed guide documents a `ddp_shard` TrainingArguments option (and a `global` / parallel_poisson accounting mode) that does not exist; its launch example raises TypeError
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced. docs/user-guide/distributed-trainer.md:41 has ddp_shard="per_rank" inside the page's only runnable TrainingArguments(...) snippet, and :46-58 is a '## ddp_shard modes' section documenting 'per_rank (default): disjoint shard per rank, Poisson accounting' and 'global: full dataset per rank with rank-folded streams and parallel_poisson accounting'. grep -rn 'ddp_shard' --include=*.py packages/ returns nothing; dataclasses.fields(TrainingArguments) has only ddp_backend and ddp_timeout; TrainingArguments(output_dir='/tmp/x', ddp_shard='per_rank') raises TypeError: unexpected keyword argument 'ddp_shard' (ran it). The trainer's world_size>1 branch (_dp_trainer.py:3886-3913) unconditionally trims and local_shards -- there is no alternative branch -- and accounting is always acc.poisson over the global rate (:1489-1494). grep also shows no parallel_poisson reference anywhere in opaque-transformers/src. History claim verified: git show 65518ae4:docs/user-guide/distributed-trainer.md already contains the ddp_shard lines (so the option never existed), and a624a34b (#1007) added five lines of per_rank divisibility prose on top of it; ba39783d (#1026) touched the page without fixing it. One extra hit the finding missed: docs/user-guide/index.md:63 also advertises 'ddp_shard behavior for DPTrainer'. Docs-only, and the broken snippet fails loudly (TypeError), so this cannot silently degrade a run; medium rather than high because the fabricated 'global'/parallel_poisson mode is the page's only statement about which amplification theorem applies to multi-GPU training. Not in either tracked-issue list.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user copies the launch snippet from docs/user-guide/distributed-trainer.md:36-44 and gets TypeError: TrainingArguments.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'ddp_shard' (reproduced); TrainingArguments exposes only ddp_backend and ddp_timeout. A reader who does not copy it instead believes two accounting modes exist -- 'per_rank' with Poisson and 'global' with full-dataset-per-rank and parallel_poisson -- when the trainer has exactly one implemented behaviour (trim to a multiple of WORLD_SIZE, disjoint local_shard, acc.poisson at the global rate) and no code path anywhere selects parallel_poisson. docs/user-guide/index.md:63 repeats the nonexistent option. Fail-loud, docs-only: no run is mis-accounted, but the page's only statement about multi-GPU amplification is unverifiable against the code, and #1007 added divisibility prose on top of the nonexistent option rather than removing it.

verdicts.title: #1008 left the sibling `save_model` barrier untouched: a saving-rank failure there still strands peers in barrier()
verdicts.reasoning: Structurally verified and reproduced end to end on 2-rank gloo. _dp_trainer.py:5036-5044: the save_model body runs 'if _distributed.should_save(a, self._ddp): ... self._save_model_artifacts(target); self._save_training_args(target); self.save_accountant(target)' with no try/except, then 'if not _internal_call: _distributed.barrier(self._ddp)'. grep confirms line 5044 is the only surviving _distributed.barrier(self._ddp) call in the trainer; the three _save_checkpoint stages use checkpoint_barrier at :5203, :5212, :5239. _distributed.py:233-243: checkpoint_barrier's docstring is exactly 'Replaces plain barrier() calls that let a saving-rank failure leave peers blocked forever', and its implementation all-reduces a failure flag so non-failing ranks raise OperationError instead of blocking -- precisely the treatment save_model does not get. I ran the finder's 2-rank gloo repro myself (TinyForCausalLM, gloo, injected _save_model_artifacts failure on rank 0): rank 0 printed 'RAISED RuntimeError: injected save_model artifact failure' while rank 1 sat in barrier() and only unblocked when rank 0's process exited, surfacing 'RuntimeError: [gloo/transport/tcp/pair.cc:545] Read error [127.0.0.1]:20194: Connection reset by peer. This is typically caused by a remote worker hanging' -- an unrelated transport error rather than any diagnostic about the failed save. Also confirmed packages/opaque-transformers/tests/distributed/_ddp_runner.py has a checkpoint-save-failure scenario but no save_model equivalent. Severity low is right: no privacy or numerical consequence, error-path-only, and it requires an actual save failure on the saving rank. Not in either tracked-issue list.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: All ranks call trainer.save_model(dir) under DDP (the documented post-training usage; the barrier comment at _dp_trainer.py:5043 presumes it). The saving rank's _save_model_artifacts / _save_training_args / save_accountant raises -- read-only or full volume, a safetensors shared-tensor error, an NFS hiccup. Because that block has no try/except and the following barrier is the plain _distributed.barrier(self._ddp) rather than checkpoint_barrier, the failing rank propagates its exception out of save_model without reaching the barrier while every peer blocks inside it. Reproduced on 2-rank gloo with an injected failure: rank 0 raised 'RuntimeError: injected save_model artifact failure'; rank 1 blocked in barrier() and only unblocked when rank 0's process died, surfacing a gloo 'Connection reset by peer' read error instead of the real cause. If the caller wraps save_model in try/except (natural for a best-effort final save) the failing rank stays alive and peers block until the store timeout. No privacy or numerical impact: the cost is a hang or a misleading transport error in place of the clean cross-rank abort #1008 introduced for the _save_checkpoint stages.
